Replace.Text: Plans the districts with the highest weighted adjacency bonus for one city, several cities or new city sites, and marks them with map tacks.

Plans districts for one city, for several cities together (wonders included) and for new city sites. Under your yield weights it looks for the plan with the highest adjacency bonus: small problems are solved exhaustively, larger ones by a search that reports how far the result may be from the best. Preview the plan, then place it as map tacks with district icons; undo is kept with the save. Placement rules and bonuses come from Detailed Map Tacks, so they match what its tacks show. Built districts and your own map tacks are never moved. Requires Detailed Map Tacks. Do not enable together with another district planner such as Auto Map Tacks Planner.

Tiles: what the tiles the districts take would have given, times this weight; 0 leaves it out. A tile counts what it gives with its best improvement; chopping and harvesting are done before building. Its yields are weighed by fixed numbers, not by the weights to the left: Food and Production 1, Science and Culture 5/6, Faith 1/2, Gold 1/4 (1 Production = 4 Gold = 2 Faith), and the same for the one-time yields of chopping and harvesting. The yields a Preserve's Grove and Sanctuary give to adjacent unimproved tiles count here too, the same way: such a tile is worth the better of its best improvement and staying unimproved with the Preserve's yields, and counts only when the city works it; only the buildings you can build now count (the Grove comes with the Preserve, the Sanctuary needs the Conservation civic).

Let districts go on tiles of your other cities: in Manage Citizens, Swap gives such a tile to this city (no district or wonder on it, not next to that city's center).[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Gain: more adjacency, measured at +13% on average for one city and +20% for several.[NEWLINE]Cost: about three in ten districts need a swap by hand; the other city loses that tile; several cities take about twice as long to plan.
One-time yields from removing Woods, Rainforest and Marsh and from harvesting Bonus resources (they grow with your technologies and civics); a tile that keeps its feature or resource forgoes them
Least work. On the offline benchmark, picking districts for one city takes about 0.1–0.2 s and reaches 98% of the best plan on average (93% at worst); four cities take about 0.5 s.
The default. On the offline benchmark, picking districts for one city takes about 0.4–1 s and always reaches the best plan; four cities take about 2–6 s.

Most work, computed over several frames; you can keep playing or close the panel meanwhile. One city takes about 2–5 s, four cities about 2–7 s, eight cities 25–60 s. On the offline benchmark it reaches the best plan as Standard does; use it when Standard says the plan may still improve.

How far each new city may be from one of your cities, a City Center map tack or another new city of the same plan, counted in tiles between the City Centers. The game needs at least 4 (3 tiles between). New cities usually land at exactly this distance: at 5 two neighbors share 4–8 tiles, at 6 their 3 rings just touch, from 7 on they share none.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]A larger number leaves each new city more tiles but fits fewer cities into the same land, and the search takes longer (about a third longer at 8 than at 5).

The plan that fits more new cities comes first (City Centers at least 3 tiles apart between them), then the one with the higher score; new cities may link on from each other. When it is on, New cities is 12 by default and can be changed; it and Max distance are kept in the save on their own, and switching it off brings the usual ones back. Tick the sites you want in the results: Place site tacks places only those.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Benefit: more cities in the same area: with the same Max distance, at most 6 usually; with it on, 12 fitted in every test.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Cost: cities close together share their tiles and resources, so each scores about 7% less on average; you tick the sites to place yourself; it takes about 1.6 times as long as 6 sites usually do.
{1_Count} new cities fit, score {2_Value}; {3_Ticked} ticked, Place site tacks places only those

Districts: the adjacency bonuses of the planned districts placed at their best around the site, less the distance cost, weighed by the yield weights in the row above. An average of +4 a planned district is 10 points.

Tiles: what the best tiles the city works once it has the planned districts yield each turn with their best improvements (Food and Production 1, Science and Culture 5/6, Faith 1/2, Gold 1/4, times the yield weights in the row above). An average of about 4.3 a worked tile at the start of the game, up to 7.2 with every technology and civic, is 10 points; it follows your progress in technologies and civics.

Features: the one-time yields of removing Woods, Rainforest and Marsh and harvesting Bonus resources within 3 tiles (they grow with your technologies and civics), spread over 50 turns; tiles the city works that are better kept do not count. About 12 Woods tiles are 10 points, about 0.8 a Woods tile, at any point of the game.

Housing: the Housing a site has over a site without water (water, Granary, and the Lighthouse and Seaport when the plan has a Harbor). A new city counts as population 1: each Housing up to the larger of 3 and one more than the population the planned districts need counts 1 (the city still grows at full speed), each one after it half the one before. 3 more (a river or lake) is 10 points.

Luxuries: the Luxury resources within 3 tiles. The first copy of a kind you lack counts the cities that get its Amenities (up to 4); each further copy counts 1, up to the number of civilizations you could sell it to (met, without that resource). A new kind for 4 cities is 10 points.

Strategics: the Strategic resource tiles within 3 tiles. Each counts 1, times 2 when the technology that reveals it is in your era or the one before; the first tile of a kind you lack counts twice that, a tile of a kind you are short of (Gathering Storm: a stockpile under a quarter of the cap, or no income) 1.5 times. A new kind revealed near your era is 10 points.
Appeal: the average Appeal of the tiles districts can take, 1 point each (off by default).

Plan as if this mod's earlier tacks for this city were gone (only the ones you have not edited), and remove them when placing the new plan; undo puts them back. Tacks you placed yourself are never touched.

Plan as if this mod's earlier tacks for the cities taking part were gone (only the ones you have not edited), and remove them when placing the new plan; undo puts them back. Tacks you placed yourself are never touched.
Shows on the map where one district is good: every tile where it can go, shaded from the best down, with the bonus of placing it there alone.

Reach: lets the plan count districts whose buildings help nearby cities, such as Factories, Power Plants, Zoos, Stadiums and Aquariums. Each of your cities or City Center map tacks newly covered adds this many points; the city being planned does not count (its own Industrial Zone always reaches it), nor does a city a district of the same kind already covers. 0 leaves it out.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Gain: covered cities get those buildings' regional effects (Production, Amenities). Measured planning one city on 42 real cities: at weight 1, 3 of them covered more cities; at weight 3, 6.[NEWLINE]Cost: those cities lost 0 to 3 adjacency (up to 4 at weight 3); planning takes about 5% longer.
Reach: this plan covers no new city

How many specialty districts this city should end up with. Districts built, under construction and map tacks for this city count, and only the rest are planned: with 2 already there and 3 chosen, 1 more is planned. The lowest number is what the city has plus the Must districts not built yet; above that the rest are picked from the pool (best gain first), and three plans with different districts are offered. 3 by default, or one more than the city has once it has 3 or more. A number you set stays with its city when you switch to another city and back.

How many specialty districts each city of this list should end up with. Districts built, under construction and map tacks for the city count, and each city plans only the rest; a city that has enough picks nothing from the pool (Must districts are still placed). A planned city has none yet and plans this many.

Must: always placed. Pool: when the count is above the required number, the best of the pool are picked. Off: left out. Districts are compared by weighted adjacency, plus tiles, reach and distance when on, plus Housing for Neighborhoods and Preserves (a Must Preserve's yields on adjacent tiles count under tiles). Encampments and Aerodromes have no adjacency bonus and are never picked from the pool: make them Must. Districts limited to one per empire (Government Plaza, Diplomatic Quarter) are Must or Off only. The Preserve starts Off, since few civilizations build it: click it to Pool or Must.

These districts have no Population requirement and do not count toward the number. Auto: added when the city needs it, placed by the solver. An Aqueduct when the city lacks fresh water (its water Housing is below the 5 a River or Lake gives); a Dam when 3 or more free Floodplains tiles lie in its 3 rings (Gathering Storm only). Left out, with a note, when it fits nowhere.

The plan's districts get adjacency bonuses from adjacent Woods and Rainforest; removing them later loses those bonuses. Placing the plan also puts a reminder tack (with the Remove Feature icon) on those tiles, named with what removing them would cost; undo removes these tacks too.
{1_Count} fewer picked: no room for more of the pool

Plans are ranked by the adjacency plus the items in brackets. Tiles is what the tiles the districts take would have given (a Preserve's extra yields on the tiles around it count here too). Late in the game the tiles often outweigh the adjacency and the sum is negative; that does not make the plan poor: districts always take tiles. Each district's own parts are on the first line of its row's tooltip.
Click to take this wonder off

Distance cost: each district and wonder loses this weight times (tiles to your nearest City Center - 1), in the same unit as adjacency, so with the same adjacency the closer tile wins; 0 is off.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Gain: a city grows outward, so its third ring comes later than its second; closer districts do not need tiles bought with Gold. On the 84 offline development scenes, 0.5 instead of 0 changed the plan in 52, moving nearly half the districts.[NEWLINE]Cost: 0.6% less adjacency on average and about 4% more lost tile yields; no extra time.
Click to switch this site on or off. Left out, no districts are planned for it and it is not counted as a new city; the tack stays where it is and still counts as a neighbor.

Must: every site is scored with it. Pool: when the count is above the required number, each site picks the best of the pool. Off: left out. The district score is the weighted adjacency less the yields of the tiles the districts take.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]By default every specialty district is in the pool, except those with no adjacency bonus and no Amenities (Preserve, Encampment, Aerodrome): they are built for what they do, so they start Off; set them to Must or Pool to count them. Districts limited to one per empire (Government Plaza) are not counted per site.
These districts have no Population requirement and do not count toward the number. Set to Must, every site places one, with its adjacency and that of the districts next to it.

How many specialty districts each site is scored with, required ones included. Above the required number each site picks the rest from the pool, best district score first; at the required number nothing is picked. At most 6.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Gain: sites scored with districts suit districts better. In 12 test scenes a count of 3, against 0 (no districts), chose other sites in 5 scenes, with 13% more adjacency in total for the districts around the sites and no scene worse.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Cost: a higher count and a larger pool take longer. In mid and late game saves a count of 0 takes about 0.1 seconds, 3 about 1 second and 6 about 1.6 seconds (Standard tier, 3 new sites); island maps are faster, about 0.4 seconds.
The {1_Building} gives +1 Trade Route capacity only in a city without a {2_Other}: a {3_A} and a {4_B} in the same city give one extra route, in two different cities two.

{1_Rules}[NEWLINE]When ticked, the pool never gives one city both; a city that already has one (built, with a map tack, or Must) does not get the other. Only when the count cannot be filled otherwise are both picked, and the result says so. Must districts are placed as asked.
the {1_Building} gives no Trade Route capacity

Housing: points per Housing. In each city, each Housing up to the larger of one more than the population its planned districts need and its population now plus 2 counts 1 (up to there the city grows at full speed), each one after it half the one before; bigger cities are discounted, since each citizen needs more Food (none up to population 5, about 0.5 at 10, 0.3 at 16). A City Center tack counts as population 1. A Neighborhood's or Preserve's Housing depends on the Appeal of its tile. The plan changes Appeal: a Holy Site or Theater Square gives adjacent tiles +1, an Industrial Zone or Encampment -1, and removing Woods -1 to the tiles around it. A Preserve's yields on adjacent tiles count under Tiles.

Farms, Pastures and similar improvements give +0.5 Housing each; the city's total is rounded down. Districts of the plan on such tiles cost the city this much Housing. Shown for information; not part of the plan's score.

Each yield of the adjacency bonuses is multiplied by its weight and the results added up; 0 leaves it out. The Tiles column weighs what the tiles the districts take would have given, its yields by fixed numbers (see its tooltip).

The sum of the parts of this city's new districts. Each district's own parts are in its row's tooltip.

Not in the districts' parts: {1_Parts}. Existing districts is the adjacency the plan adds to the districts already there and to locked map tacks. Tiles, Housing and reach go to each district as how much the part comes back when that district alone is left out; when several districts compete for the same tiles, their shares fall short of the total by this much.
